structure: Part 11, "Port of entry, arrival and transit countries": the first two pages of the live-animals transport-and-arrival section. Read in full: features/transport/port-of-entry/ (port-of-entry.controller.js, port-of-entry.njk, arrival-window.js, validate.js — the *.test.js unit tests left out by the scope), features/transport/transit-countries/ (transit-countries.controller.js, transit-countries.njk, _added-countries-table.njk, rows.js, remove-action.js, validate.js — likewise), the shared feature files features/transport/page.js, evaluation.js, means-of-transport-label.js, copy/copy.en.js and copy/copy.cy.js (claiming only the portOfEntry and transitCountries key trees, with one parity claim on the Welsh file), features/transport/fit/arrival-transit.fit.spec.js (1,191 lines, 41 tests across 11 describe blocks: arrival rendering, port type-ahead, port without JavaScript, arrival date calendar, arrival validation, transport reference validation, arrival save and routing, arrival continue with no commodity, transit rendering and validation, transit list/limits/persistence, Save and continue order, transit without JavaScript, and accessibility) and features/transport/fit/test-support.js, which holds only transporter form fixtures and so yields nothing for these two pages (parts 12 and 13 own it). Read for context, not claimed beyond what these two pages show: fit/live-animals-journey.js helpers (openArrival, openTransit, LANDINGS, ARRIVAL_DATE_IN_WINDOW, answerArrivalDetails, answerTransitCountries, addTransitCountry), shared/kit.js (dateField, pageRoutes, saveActions), shared/paths.js, shared/copy.en.js (dateExample, validatorDefaults, saveActions), services/ports/, services/transport-reference/, services/countries/, lib/validate/calendar.js, flow/flow.js, flow/task-rows.js, flow/section-captions/ and obligations/sections/arrival.js and transport.js. Covered: both pages' routes, captions, headings, every field with its label, hint, component and limits, the arrival window, every validation message verbatim, the add-and-remove table and its limit, where Save and continue and Save and return lead, the no-JavaScript fallbacks, the accessibility assertions, and the obligation and task-row gating that decides whether transit countries is asked at all.

claims.statement: Both pages offer the same three save controls: a "Save and continue" button, a secondary "Save and return to overview" button, and a "Cancel and return to overview" link to the overview.
Save and continue from arrival details opens the transit countries page when the means of transport is rail or road, and the transporter list when it is air or sea.

Saving arrival details by road while only the country of origin has been answered opens the "What are you importing?" commodity search instead of the next transport page, and the overview offers no transit countries row until a commodity is saved.
Saving arrival details and returning to the overview keeps all five answers: reopening the page shows the date, port, means, identification and document reference as saved.
A refused save on either page re-renders the page with the error summary and answers the user typed, and answers HTTP 400.
When the save itself cannot be made, both pages come back with a recoverable-error notice and answer HTTP 500 rather than losing the user's place.
Both pages carry a Back link that returns to the overview when the page was opened from its overview task.

claims.statement: The countries added so far are carried in the page's own form, so a country is listed only while the page is open and is kept only when the user saves.

claims.statement: Transit countries saves one answer, transitedCountries, as the list of country codes in the order they were added.
Transit countries are optional: Save and return to overview with none added saves the notification with no error and the page reopens empty.
Transit countries is asked only of a consignment arriving by rail or road: for any other means of transport the answer is out of scope and dropped.
The overview shows a transit countries task row only while the page applies, which is why the row is marked conditional.
Opening the transit countries page by its address when it does not apply sends the user to the overview, and the service logs why.
Adding a country on a transit countries page left open after the means of transport changed to air sends the user to the overview rather than adding it.
When an answer the transit countries page needs has not been given yet, the user is sent to the page that asks for it, with the back trail carried, and the service logs which answers were missing.
Save and continue from transit countries opens the transporter list.

Saving transit countries and returning to the overview keeps the countries added, listed again in the same order and under the same names when the page is reopened, with the status announcement cleared.

claims.statement: Every English copy key these two pages use has a Welsh counterpart in the same shape, machine-drafted and not yet signed off by a translator.

claims.statement: The transit countries page offers no confirmation step for adding or removing a country, and no "are you sure" page: the table is the whole interaction.
claims.note: Follows because both the add and the remove action render the same page back with the list changed; no other route or template exists in the feature folder for a confirmation.
